changes.content:
# Personal calendar reminders

An authenticated participant or staff user can choose a date and explicitly consent to export a generic all-day `.ics` reminder from a currently accessible record. Export rechecks record access immediately before preparing the download. Navigating away suppresses a held response; a denied access check produces no file. No calendar provider is called and no server record, notice, legal-service state or legal deadline is changed.

The strict writer accepts only a chosen date and affirmative consent. The file contains a generic title/description, chosen date, generation timestamp, independent random event identifier and software identifier. It contains no case title/text/identifier, person/contact/location, evidence reference, attachment, organizer, attendee or workspace URL. `CLASS:PRIVATE` is an advisory classification, not encryption or a provider guarantee. The consent text explains provider/shared-calendar visibility and that imported copies cannot be recalled. Users choose calendar notifications themselves; export does not establish delivery. Repeated downloads in the same open form and date reuse the file identifier, without claiming that every importer deduplicates.

Dates are validated as real calendar days; leap days, year boundaries and an exclusive following-day end are handled without timezone conversion. Year overflow is rejected. Lines use CRLF, are folded at 75 UTF-8 octets without splitting characters, and reject control-character injection. Free text and additional input fields are not accepted.

Standards basis: RFC 5545 sections 3.1, 3.6.1, 3.8.2.2, 3.8.2.4, 3.8.4.7 and 3.8.7.2, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545.html. Calendar privacy and delivery behavior still depend on the user's chosen application.

Verification: `tests/reminders.test.ts` tests dates, explicit consent, strict input, independent identifiers, injection and UTF-8 folding. `tests/private/reminders.spec.ts` exercises consent, bytes, repeated export, denied access, late response after navigation, accessibility and responsive layout on desktop/mobile. On October 12, 2026, all 134 unit tests and the API, worker, portal and staff builds passed locally, along with formatting, boundary and source checks. Remote browser execution and screenshot inspection remain separate evidence gates. This completes a personal preparation helper, not the legal deadline/notice integration workstream.

## Personal reminder development

A privacy-minimal all-day calendar export is implemented for explicit personal use. It rechecks current record access, suppresses a response after navigation and excludes case information. No provider is called and no legal deadline or service is established. Unit and desktop/mobile failure-path coverage is in `PERSONAL_REMINDERS.md`; remote acceptance remains a merge gate.
